sentences.text: Acristavus is a genus of saurolophine dinosaur, a name that translates to "non-crested grandfather".
Unlike nearly all other hadrosaurids, this animal lacked skull ornamentation and grew to be 8.5 meters long, 2.5 meters tall, and weigh roughly 2.5 tonnes.
This species is significant because it implies that the common ancestor of all duck-billed dinosaurs did not have cranial decorations.
A fossil trackway found in 2010 indicates that primitive mammals and dinosaurs interacted as predators and prey in this region.
The type species A. gagslarsoni was named in 2011 based on the holotype specimen MOR 1155, which was recovered from the Two Medicine Formation in Teton County, Montana.

This holotype includes an almost complete skull along with eleven neck vertebrae and various limb parts, while a second specimen, UMNHVP 16607, was assigned to the genus in the same year after being dug up in Utah.
Currently, there are only two recorded fossil occurrences of this dinosaur.
Acristavus belongs to the family Hadrosauridae and the class Ornithischia.

Researchers initially assigned the animal to the basal position within the Brachylophosaurini tribe, and subsequent phylogenetic analyses have confirmed that it belongs to this group of derived members within the Saurolophinae subfamily.

It is debated whether Acristavus and Maiasaura are sister taxa, as Gates concluded they share a relationship, but a more recent analysis by Prieto-Márquez suggests Maiasaura is more closely related to the advanced Brachylophosaurus.
The holotype was collected from rock deposited during the Campanian stage of the Cretaceous, a period spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.

At that time, the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest, isolating southern Laramidia, and the Wahweap Formation where fossils were found has been radiometrically dated between 81 and 76 million years ago.
Acristavus inhabited an environment containing lakes, floodplains, and east-flowing rivers, where rapid sedimentation suggests a humid, seasonal climate.

In the Wahweap Formation, it coexisted with the ceratopsian Diabloceratops, the lambeosaurine Adelolophus, the tyrannosaurid Lythronax argestes, freshwater fish, rays, sharks, turtles like Compsemys, crocodilians, and lungfish.
